findings.finding: Peer Veidekke's Q3 2026 (released 12 Nov) showed pre-tax profit NOK 904m vs 721m, margin 7.7% vs 6.8%, with the improvement 'particularly strong in Norway, in both building and infrastructure' and 12-month executable orders +14% - a direct read-through to AFG's Norwegian Civil Engineering, Construction and Betonmast segments.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AFG beat Yahoo EPS consensus on all four of the last four quarters (+0.4%, +20%, +7%, +23%) and the stock moved +6.5%, -3.7%, +5.5%, +2.35% on those prints - beats mostly rewarded, one sold (Q4 2025).
findings.original_quote: Resultatforbedringen i kvartalet var særlig sterk i Norge, både for bygg- og infrastrukturvirksomheten (The profit improvement in the quarter was particularly strong in Norway, both for the building and the infrastructure business)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Veidekke closed +1.8% on 12 Nov (Yahoo VEI.OL 223 -> 227) while AFG closed flat at 205, so the market did not mark AFG up on the read-through that day - but AFG had already run +4.5% from 6 to 11 Nov into the print. Proxy evidence (a peer, not AFG's own number), so held small.
findings.independence: Veidekke's 21 Oct market report raised its Scandinavian construction growth forecast to 7% for 2026 with Norway at 7%: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=684454

findings.finding: Veidekke's October market analysis says Norwegian residential construction is still expected to fall, with higher rates and many unsold homes delaying recovery - consistent with AFG's own Q2 Property segment (weak result, 23 units sold vs 61, 111 completed unsold units).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Property has been weak in Q3 2025 and Q2 2026 releases without driving the reaction (Q3 2025 +6.5%, Q2 2026 +2.35%); it is a small segment.
findings.original_quote: i Norge ventes boligproduksjonen fortsatt å falle ... økte renter og mange usolgte boliger bidrar til å forsinke oppgangen (in Norway housing production is expected to keep falling ... higher rates and many unsold homes delay the upturn)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: weak Property was already flagged by AFG itself in Q2 and the segment is small net of the rest of the company (Civil Engineering, Betonmast, Energy and Environment, Offshore carry the result). Kept as a small offset.
findings.independence: AFG's own Q2 2026 release: 'Property reported a weak result in the quarter' https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=681086

findings.finding: An aggregator lists an AFG ex-dividend date of 18 Nov 2026, implying the board will declare its customary autumn dividend with the Q3 report; balance sheet supports it (net interest-bearing receivable NOK 131m at Q2, buyback ended 25 Sep).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 release carried an additional NOK 4.00 dividend and the stock rose 6.5% that day (not separable from the beat).
findings.why_not_priced: The autumn dividend is a routine, expected event, so only a surprise in size would move the stock; snippet-only date, not confirmed in an issuer document, so held small.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 release: additional NOK 4.00 dividend approved https://www.afgruppen.com/news/2025/11/revenue-growth-and-good-results-in-the-third-quarter/

findings.finding: 1,018 employees subscribed 1,000,000 shares in the annual employee share programme at NOK 150.26 (20% discount), completed 30 Oct; 685,225 new shares issued (+0.6% dilution), treasury shares now zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Annual routine programme; no measurable reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 8 Oct and routine; what the money buys is employee alignment, not a capex need. Broad, full subscription is a mild internal-confidence signal only.
